passages.text: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.
passages.sermon:
The prophet speaks to a city.
This city is violent.
This city is called the city of blood.
This city is full of lies.
This city is full of stolen goods.
This city always has victims.
This city never stops preying on others.
passages.original: ה֖וֹי עִ֣יר דָּמִ֑ים כֻּלָּ֗הּ כַּ֤חַשׁ פֶּ֙רֶק֙ מְלֵאָ֔ה לֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ טָֽרֶף׃

passages.text: The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!
passages.sermon:
This passage describes a scene of battle and chaos.
\r\nYou hear the crack of the whip.
\r\nYou hear the rumble of the wheel.
\r\nA horse gallops.
\r\nA chariot bounds forward.
passages.original: ק֣וֹל שׁ֔וֹט וְק֖וֹל רַ֣עַשׁ אוֹפָ֑ן וְס֣וּס דֹּהֵ֔ר וּמֶרְכָּבָ֖ה מְרַקֵּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end— they stumble over their dead— because of the many harlotries of the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery, who betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft.
passages.sermon:
Nineveh is a city full of blood.
Nineveh is full of lies and plunder.
Nineveh is never without prey.
Horsemen charge into battle.
Swords flash.
Spears shine.
There are heaps of slain people.
There are mounds of corpses.
There is no end to the dead bodies.
People stumble over the dead.
This happens because of the many harlotries of the harlot.
She is a seductive woman.
She practices sorcery.
She sells nations through her prostitution.
She enslaves clans by her witchcraft.
passages.original: פָּרָ֣שׁ מַעֲלֶ֗ה וְלַ֤הַב חֶ֙רֶב֙ וּבְרַ֣ק חֲנִ֔ית וְרֹ֥ב חָלָ֖ל וְכֹ֣בֶד פָּ֑גֶר וְאֵ֥ין קֵ֙צֶה֙ לַגְּוִיָּ֔ה יִכְשְׁלוּ בִּגְוִיָּתָֽם׃ מֵרֹב֙ זְנוּנֵ֣י זוֹנָ֔ה ט֥וֹבַת חֵ֖ן בַּעֲלַ֣ת כְּשָׁפִ֑ים הַמֹּכֶ֤רֶת גּוֹיִם֙ בִּזְנוּנֶ֔יהָ וּמִשְׁפָּח֖וֹת בִּכְשָׁפֶֽיהָ׃

passages.text: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks.
The LORD of Hosts is powerful and commands armies.
The LORD of Hosts says, “I am against you.”
I will lift your skirts over your face.
I will expose your nakedness to the nations.
I will show your shame to the kingdoms.
passages.original: הִנְנִ֣י אֵלַ֗יִךְ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְגִלֵּיתִ֥י שׁוּלַ֖יִךְ עַל־ פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְהַרְאֵיתִ֤י גוֹיִם֙ מַעְרֵ֔ךְ וּמַמְלָכ֖וֹת קְלוֹנֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make a spectacle of you.
passages.sermon:
The LORD of Hosts speaks to Nineveh.
The LORD says, “I am against you.”
I will throw filth on you.
I will treat you with contempt.
I will make you a spectacle before others.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁלַכְתִּ֥י עָלַ֛יִךְ שִׁקֻּצִ֖ים וְנִבַּלְתִּ֑יךְ וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּרֹֽאִי׃

passages.text: Then all who see you will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’ Where can I find comforters for you?”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Nineveh.
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God says He is against Nineveh.
God says He will punish Nineveh.
Everyone who sees Nineveh will turn away from her.
They will not want to come near her.
They will say, “Nineveh is destroyed.”
They will ask, “Who will mourn for Nineveh?”
They will say, “Where can I find anyone to comfort you, Nineveh?”
passages.original: וְהָיָ֤ה כָל־ רֹאַ֙יִךְ֙ יִדּ֣וֹד מִמֵּ֔ךְ וְאָמַר֙ שָׁדְּדָ֣ה נִֽינְוֵ֔ה מִ֖י יָנ֣וּד לָ֑הּ מֵאַ֛יִן אֲבַקֵּ֥שׁ מְנַחֲמִ֖ים לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: Are you better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Nineveh.
God asks Nineveh a question.
God says, “Are you better than Thebes?”
Thebes was a great city.
Thebes sat by the Nile River.
Water surrounded Thebes.
The sea was Thebes’ defense.
Water was Thebes’ wall.
passages.original: הֲתֵֽיטְבִי֙ מִנֹּ֣א אָמ֔וֹן הַיֹּֽשְׁבָה֙ בַּיְאֹרִ֔ים מַ֖יִם סָבִ֣יב לָ֑הּ אֲשֶׁר־ חֵ֣יל יָ֔ם מִיָּ֖ם חוֹמָתָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
passages.sermon:
Thebes was a powerful city.
Cush gave her great strength.
Egypt also gave her strength.
Their support had no limit.
Put helped her.
Libya helped her.
These nations were her allies.
passages.original: כּ֥וּשׁ עָצְמָ֛ה וּמִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֵ֣ין קֵ֑צֶה פּ֣וּט וְלוּבִ֔ים הָי֖וּ בְּעֶזְרָתֵֽךְ׃

passages.text: Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her dignitaries, and all her nobles were bound in chains.
passages.sermon:
Thebes was a great city in Egypt.
Thebes had many allies and strong defenses.
Yet Thebes became an exile.
Thebes went into captivity.
Enemies killed her infants at the head of every street.
Enemies cast lots for her dignitaries.
Enemies bound all her nobles in chains.
passages.original: גַּם־ הִ֗יא לַגֹּלָה֙ הָלְכָ֣ה בַשֶּׁ֔בִי גַּ֧ם עֹלָלֶ֛יהָ יְרֻטְּשׁ֖וּ בְּרֹ֣אשׁ כָּל־ חוּצ֑וֹת וְעַל־ נִכְבַּדֶּ֙יהָ֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל וְכָל־ גְּדוֹלֶ֖יהָ רֻתְּק֥וּ בַזִּקִּֽים׃

passages.text: You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to Nineveh.
Nineveh is proud and powerful.
But Nineveh will fall.
You also will become drunk.
You will lose control.
You will go into hiding.
You will try to escape.
You will seek safety from your enemy.
passages.original: גַּם־ אַ֣תְּ תִּשְׁכְּרִ֔י תְּהִ֖י נַֽעֲלָמָ֑ה גַּם־ אַ֛תְּ תְּבַקְשִׁ֥י מָע֖וֹז מֵאוֹיֵֽב׃

passages.text: All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!
passages.sermon:
The prophet Nahum speaks to Nineveh.
Nineveh has many strong fortresses.
These fortresses are like fig trees.
The fig trees have early, ripe figs.
If someone shakes the trees, the figs fall down.
The figs fall straight into the mouth of the one who eats them.
Your fortresses will fall easily, just like these figs.
passages.original: כָּ֨ל־ מִבְצָרַ֔יִךְ תְּאֵנִ֖ים עִם־ בִּכּוּרִ֑ים אִם־ יִנּ֕וֹעוּ וְנָפְל֖וּ עַל־ פִּ֥י אוֹכֵֽל׃

passages.text: Look at your troops— they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.
passages.sermon:
Your troops are inside your city.
Your troops are weak like women.
Your enemies stand outside your land.
The gates of your land are open to your enemies.
Fire burns the bars of your gates.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֨ה עַמֵּ֤ךְ נָשִׁים֙ בְּקִרְבֵּ֔ךְ לְאֹ֣יְבַ֔יִךְ פָּת֥וֹחַ נִפְתְּח֖וּ שַׁעֲרֵ֣י אַרְצֵ֑ךְ אָכְלָ֥ה אֵ֖שׁ בְּרִיחָֽיִך׃

passages.text: Draw your water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln!
passages.sermon:
The prophet Nahum speaks to the city of Nineveh.
Nineveh faces an enemy siege.
Prepare for the attack.
Draw water for yourself.
Strengthen your fortresses.
Go into the clay.
Tread the mortar.
Make the brick kiln strong.
Work hard to defend your city.
passages.original: מֵ֤י מָצוֹר֙ שַֽׁאֲבִי־ לָ֔ךְ חַזְּקִ֖י מִבְצָרָ֑יִךְ בֹּ֧אִי בַטִּ֛יט וְרִמְסִ֥י בַחֹ֖מֶר הַחֲזִ֥יקִי מַלְבֵּֽן׃

passages.text: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you down and consume you like a young locust. Make yourself many like the young locust; make yourself many like the swarming locust!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Nineveh.
God warns them of coming destruction.
Fire will devour you there.
The sword will cut you down.
The sword will consume you like a young locust.
Multiply yourself like the young locust.
Increase your numbers like the swarming locust.
passages.original: שָׁ֚ם תֹּאכְלֵ֣ךְ אֵ֔שׁ תַּכְרִיתֵ֣ךְ חֶ֔רֶב תֹּאכְלֵ֖ךְ כַּיָּ֑לֶק הִתְכַּבֵּ֣ד כַּיֶּ֔לֶק הִֽתְכַּבְּדִ֖י כָּאַרְבֶּֽה׃

passages.text: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips the land and flies away.
passages.sermon:
Assyria has many merchants.
Assyria has more merchants than the stars in the sky.
A young locust comes.
The young locust strips the land.
The young locust flies away.
passages.original: הִרְבֵּית֙ רֹֽכְלַ֔יִךְ מִכּוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם יֶ֥לֶק פָּשַׁ֖ט וַיָּעֹֽף׃

passages.text: Your guards are like the swarming locust, and your scribes like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria has guards.
His guards are like swarming locusts.
He has scribes.
His scribes are like clouds of locusts.
The locusts settle on the walls on a cold day.
When the sun rises, the locusts fly away.
No one knows where the locusts go.
passages.original: מִנְּזָרַ֙יִךְ֙ כָּֽאַרְבֶּ֔ה וְטַפְסְרַ֖יִךְ כְּג֣וֹב גֹּבָ֑י הַֽחוֹנִ֤ים בַּגְּדֵרוֹת֙ בְּי֣וֹם קָרָ֔ה שֶׁ֤מֶשׁ זָֽרְחָה֙ וְנוֹדַ֔ד וְלֹֽא־ נוֹדַ֥ע מְקוֹמ֖וֹ אַיָּֽם׃

passages.text: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your officers sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.
passages.sermon:
The king of Assyria rules over his people.
His shepherds sleep.
His officers rest.
His people are scattered on the mountains.
No one gathers them.
passages.original: נָמ֤וּ רֹעֶ֙יךָ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר יִשְׁכְּנ֖וּ אַדִּירֶ֑יךָ נָפֹ֧שׁוּ עַמְּךָ֛ עַל־ הֶהָרִ֖ים וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּֽץ׃

passages.text: There is no healing for your injury; your wound is severe. All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall, for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?
passages.sermon:
The prophet speaks to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria is cruel.
The king of Assyria has caused much suffering.
Your injury cannot be healed.
Your wound is very severe.
Everyone who hears about you claps their hands at your fall.
They are glad because you are defeated.
You have always done evil to everyone.
No one has escaped your cruelty.
Everyone has suffered from your actions.
passages.original: אֵין־ כֵּהָ֣ה לְשִׁבְרֶ֔ךָ נַחְלָ֖ה מַכָּתֶ֑ךָ כֹּ֣ל׀ שֹׁמְעֵ֣י שִׁמְעֲךָ֗ תָּ֤קְעוּ כַף֙ עָלֶ֔יךָ כִּ֗י עַל־ מִ֛י לֹֽא־ עָבְרָ֥ה רָעָתְךָ֖ תָּמִֽיד׃
